slides.1.title: Level 1 key points
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Vine and climate
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Budburst at about 10°C; flowering weather decides yield; malic acid falls fast in warm climates; about 0.6°C cooler per 100 m; cold currents cool coasts
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Viticulture and disease
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Bush vines resist drought, trellises suit machines; phylloxera answered by grafting; sulphur for powdery mildew, copper for downy; leafroll spread by mealybugs
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Winemaking
slides.1.highlights.2.content: MLF lowers acidity and may add butter; four rosé methods; carbonic maceration gives soft fruitiness; cold stabilisation prevents tartrates; TCA is linked to natural cork
slides.1.content: Answer with “condition → mechanism → result”: the easiest way to score.

Poor weather at flowering most directly affects what?
Which of these cools a coastal region?
Cold currents and sea fog cool coasts.
What is the main effect of poor soils on the vine?
D. Controls vigour and raises concentration
Fertile soils tend to drive excess vigour.
What is powdery mildew usually controlled with?
Which of these is allowed in organic viticulture?
Organic bans synthetic pesticides and fertilisers.
To make Chardonnay rounder and more buttery, what can be done?
C. Allow MLF and stir the lees
D. Cool stainless steel and block MLF
MLF and bâtonnage add roundness and butteriness.
B. No skin contact at all
D. The rosé is a by-product that also concentrates the red
The red left behind has a higher skin-to-juice ratio.
What risk is most often mentioned for screwcaps?
The tight seal makes small amounts of sulphides harder to dissipate.
